text.p: LME copper and aluminium finished Wednesday's afternoon kerb softer, but failed to break out of price bands which have imprisoned the market recently. Most other metals fell under the moderately bearish influence and also ended the day easier, but business was thin ahead of the long Easter break.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index was 0.42 points higher at 245.91.

In London, three months copper slid after failing again at the upside in the morning, stalling at a high of $2,385, the region that has capped prices for the past two weeks. But the market lacked the steam to break substantially lower, ending the day at its low of $2,352, off $25.

Fund profit-taking pressured aluminium, which ended the kerb at $1,632, down $21. The final price was $2 off its low, which was the lowest price since February 21 and below the 30-day moving average. Balancing the fund liquidation, however, was some forward and trade buying, which was encouraging, Squires said.
Investment funds were also locking in profits and scaling down long positions in nickel, Squires said, adding that the broad uptrends in both metals were still intact.
Nickel finished $145 lower at $7,635. Support was pegged at $7,600, chartists said.
Lead tried higher, touching $687, but ended just $1 firmer at $680, its 30-day moving average.
Zinc shed $10 to $1,289 after failing to attack the $1,300 level earlier in the day.
Tin finished $20 weaker at $5,825, closing just off its low.
Alloy ended slightly easier at $1,540, down from $1,545/55.

CBOT wheat futures were higher at midsession on commercial short covering ahead of Monday's USDA quarterly stocks and planting intentions report, traders said."The commercials are a little nervous about going into the (USDA) report short," a floor trader said. At 1040 CST, wheat was up seven to five cents per bushel with May up seven at $3.96-1/2.

NYMEX crude oil prices began to fall off their midday highs ahead of the close on Wednesday but remained strong despite a lack of volume, players said. "We ran up to highs in crude earlier today," said one New York floor trader. "But once we got up to those highs the marketstalled. There is a real lack of volume." At 1414 EST/1914 GMT, May crude was trading 17 cents higher at $21.16 a barrel after hitting a high today of $21.42.

New York precious metals reversed mid-session to move higher, drawing strength from COMEX May silver's determination not to break below the key $5.10 an ounce level, traders said. Silver's resilience to hold this level prompted earlier shortcovering, which later spilled over into gold, pulling up the latter along with the white metals, traders said. "The locals tripped over themselves and found they were a little oversold, and we also had a little light fund buying," John Geraghty of North American Equity Services said. At 1219 EST COMEX June gold was up $0.80 at $351.30.
